judged_text: The duplicate-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive while the blacklist comparison lowercases the list entry, so the filter is inconsistent on email case. Submitting `Guest@Example.com` when `guest@example.com` is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (two ICS attendees, two emails to the same person), and `Guest@Example.com` bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist because the comparison compares a raw-case guest against lowercased entries.

Submitting `Guest@Example.com` when `guest@example.com` is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (two ICS attendees, two emails to the same person), and `Guest@Example.com` bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist because the comparison compares a raw-case guest against lowercased entries.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with case-sensitive comparisons: it checks duplicates via `guest === attendee.email` and blacklist via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since the blacklist is lowercased (`.map(email => email.toLowerCase())`) but `guest` is not normalized, a differently-cased email (e.g. `Guest@Example.com`) can bypass both the existing-attendee duplicate check and the blacklist, leading to duplicate attendee rows and unintended emails.
